title.en: Describe HTTP, FTP, PPP, SMTP and TCP/IP

say.en: Two people who speak different languages cannot talk. Two computers need a shared language too: a protocol. Different jobs, like sending mail or loading a page, use different protocols. In this lesson: State why protocols are needed.
Describe HTTP, FTP, PPP, SMTP and TCP/IP.

body.en: A protocol is a set of standard rules that sender and receiver follow so that they can communicate correctly. *Protocols* define the format of data, how errors are detected, how fast to send (flow control) and how to start and end communication. Devices made by different companies can talk to each other only because they follow the same protocols.

narration.en: Protocols are agreed rules for communication. They fix the data format, error checking and speed, so devices from different makers can work together.
narration.kn: ಶಿಷ್ಟಾಚಾರಗಳು ಸಂವಹನದ ಒಪ್ಪಿತ ನಿಯಮಗಳು. ದತ್ತಾಂಶ ರೂಪ, ದೋಷ ಪರಿಶೀಲನೆ, ವೇಗವನ್ನು ನಿಗದಿಪಡಿಸಿ ಬೇರೆ ಕಂಪನಿಗಳ ಸಾಧನಗಳು ಒಟ್ಟಿಗೆ ಕೆಲಸ ಮಾಡುವಂತೆ ಮಾಡುತ್ತವೆ.

title.en: On the board: HTTP requests and TCP/IP packets

say.en: A protocol is a set of rules both sides follow. In HTTP, the browser sends a request and the server sends a response.
TCP splits the page into numbered packets and makes sure all arrive, in order. IP addresses and routes each packet.
Other protocols do other jobs.

prompt.en: Match each protocol with the job it does.

right.en: Carries web pages between a browser and a web server
Transfers files between a client and a server
Links two nodes directly, such as a computer and its ISP, with authentication
Breaks a message into packets and reassembles them reliably and in order
Gives addresses and routes each packet to its destination

explanation.en: Protocols are agreed rules. HTTP is for the web, FTP for files, SMTP for sending mail and PPP for a direct link; in TCP/IP, TCP makes delivery reliable and IP handles addressing and routing.

say.en: Which protocol? Match each protocol with the job it does.

title.en: HTTP, FTP, PPP, SMTP and TCP/IP

body.en: HTTP: transfers web pages between browser (client) and web server using requests and responses. FTP: transfers files between a client and a server. PPP: connects two nodes directly (point to point), e.g. a computer to an ISP, with authentication. SMTP: sends e-mail from client to server and between mail servers. TCP/IP: the Internet's core suite; TCP breaks messages into packets and reassembles them reliably and in order, while IP gives addresses and routes each packet.

points.en: PPP: direct link between two nodes
TCP: reliable packets; IP: addressing and routing

narration.en: HTTP is for web pages, FTP for files, PPP for a direct link between two nodes, SMTP for sending mail, and TCP/IP carries everything on the Internet.

problem.en: Name the protocol used in each step: (i) Asha opens a college website, (ii) she e-mails her project to her lecturer, (iii) the lecturer uploads results to the college server, (iv) every one of these messages is split into packets and routed.

steps.en: (i) Fetching a web page → HTTP (HTTPS when secure).
(iii) Uploading a file to a server → FTP.
(iv) Packets and routing underneath everything → TCP/IP.

narration.en: Let us work through this together. Name the protocol used in each step: (i) Asha opens a college website, (ii) she e-mails her project to her lecturer, (iii) the lecturer uploads results to the college server, (iv) every one of these messages is split into packets and routed.

say.en: Let us work through this together. Name the protocol used in each step: i Asha opens a college website, ii she e-mails her project to her lecturer, iii the lecturer uploads results to the college server, iv every one of these messages is split into packets and routed.
i Fetching a web page gives HTTP HTTPS when secure.
ii Sending e-mail gives SMTP.
iii Uploading a file to a server gives FTP.
iv Packets and routing underneath everything gives TCP/IP.
So the answer is i HTTP, ii SMTP, iii FTP, iv TCP/IP.
